scenes.headline: $8 billion of customer money. Gone.
scenes.voiceover: In twenty twenty-two, one of the world's biggest crypto exchanges collapsed in a matter of days. And around eight billion dollars of customer money was missing.

scenes.headline: No independent board. No real controls.
scenes.voiceover: Its founder was a billionaire celebrity, but there was no real independent board, and the controls were weak. Customer money was moved to Alameda Research, a trading firm he also controlled.

scenes.name: FTX
scenes.headline: Customers asked for their money back
scenes.voiceover: When questions came out about Alameda's finances, customers rushed to withdraw. F T X couldn't pay them.

scenes.headline: The money wasn't there.
scenes.voiceover: Within days, F T X was bankrupt.

scenes.name: FTX
scenes.headline: 25 years. Appeal rejected in 2026.
scenes.voiceover: Sam Bankman-Fried was convicted of fraud and sentenced to twenty-five years in prison. His appeal failed in June twenty twenty-six.

scenes.headline: Technology doesn't create governance.
scenes.voiceover: The lesson? Technology doesn't create governance. If nobody independently controls the money, it can disappear.
